newsitem.title: CANADA: B.C. lumber firms plan final labor contract offer.
newsitem.headline: B.C. lumber firms plan final labor contract offer.

text.p: British Columbia coastal forestry companies have drafted a final contract proposal they plan to present to the union representing lumberworkers, the chief negotiator for the companies said Thursday.
"We'll be giving them our final position...We are not going to improve on it," said Keith Bennett of Forest Industrial Relations which bargains on behalf of 65 companies.
Officials of the IWA-Canada union were not available for comment.
Bennett said a time for a meeting between the two sides had not yet been fixed, but a session was possible later Thursday. He declined to discuss details of the companies' contract offer.
A main outstanding issue in the talks was wages. A gap of four percentage points divided the wage increase last offered by the companies and the pay increase demanded by the union.
The two sides have been bargaining on a new three-year deal to replace a contract that expired June 14.
